before.name: Head, jawline and external landmarks
before.description: A robust balaenid with an arched mouth, narrow dorsal rostrum, wide paddle-shaped flippers and no dorsal fin. The pale head callosities are rough skin colonized by cyamids; their patterns identify individuals, not a universal species template. Selected external reconstructions are not measured internal anatomy.

before.name: Horizontal flukes and caudal peduncle
before.description: Selected horizontal flukes articulate dorsoventrally with the posterior body. Planform, excursion, tissue limits and optical response are authored and unmeasured; no computed thrust or hydrodynamic validation.

before.name: Dorsal exterior and species-specific appendages
before.description: Selected fin, ridge or finless dorsal region follows this species account. Flipper proportions and visible marks are selected external comparisons, not universal diagnostics or fitted specimen dimensions.

after.name: Arched jaw and cyamid-colonized callosities
after.description: A large head with a narrow arched rostrum and strongly bowed lower lips. The selected Atlantic appearance has elongated, broken pale rostral bands and separate chin, lip and eye-region callosities guided by the NOAA mother-and-calf aerial photograph. The pale areas are roughened skin occupied by light whale lice, not generic white barnacle shells. The pattern is individual; the reconstruction does not identify the photographed whale.

after.name: Broad black flukes and narrow tail stock
after.description: A broad horizontal tail with a central notch and smooth trailing margins, joined to a tapering caudal peduncle. The selected source-derived planform is shared with the right-whale body plan; authored flexion is not a measured thrust or tissue solution.

after.name: Stocky body, finless back and broad flippers
after.description: A robust dark adult body with no dorsal fin or rorqual throat grooves, and relatively short, broad paddle-shaped pectoral flippers. The two northern models have modestly different selected fullness. External proportions and marks overlap among right-whale species; neither body condition nor callosity location establishes ocean-basin identity.
